Subject: Initial DPA + questions on role mapping and subprocessors

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ACME's legal and procurement teams reviewed the template DPA and had a few focused questions before we send redlines back. High-level: we need clarity on (1) explicit role assignment (controller vs. processor) for embeddings and telemetry, (2) a current subprocessor registry for inference and metrics pipelines, and (3) the expected data residency for logs shipped to your telemetry service.

I've attached our initial checklist and a slightly annotated copy of your standard DPA (ACME_DPA_20270601-initial.docx). Can your privacy team confirm:
- Do you consider embeddings created by model inference to be customer data subject to the DPA?
- Are telemetry logs containing request metadata treated as "operational logs" (processor-only) or could Redwood assert controller responsibilities in any circumstances?
- Will there be any cross-border transfers outside the US for data classification purposes (EU transfers)?

We want to avoid surprises during procurement. If it's easier, happy to route an initial redline for sign-off via DocuSign once we align.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe
ACME Corp — Legal

Jane —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then Ill loop in Marissa (Legal) and Rishi (Security/Privacy):

- Embeddings: treated as customer data under the DPA. We do not claim any ownership; we surface this in the DPA definition set.
- Telemetry/logs: default is processor-only. We collect telemetry for service reliability; we can provide anonymization/pseudonymization options and a retention window that ACME can set.
- Transfers: hosted inference for your org will be US-only unless you opt into cross-region replication. For EU residency we can discuss a Dedicated or Private deployment.

I'll attach our canonical subprocessor registry and propose a short standing call to walk through redlines.

Avery

Subject: Re: Initial DPA + questions on role mapping and subprocessors

Hi Jane,

Following up with more formal language you can expect in the DPA and an inline note about controller/processor mapping. Key points:

1) Definitions: we will add an explicit definition that "Customer Data" includes model inputs and any derived artifacts such as embeddings that are attributable to the customer's requests. This resolves the embeddings ownership question.

2) Roles: Redwood is the processor for data processed to provide inference services. The exception clause will be narrow: if Redwood receives court-ordered requests for customer data relevant to our operations, we will notify ACME unless prohibited. We will not assert controller status for routine telemetry.

3) Telemetry & logs: operational telemetry (latency, error rates, anonymized routing ids) is treated as service reliability data. For any logs that could identify individuals (IP, user_id), we can either pseudonymize before storage or apply a shorter retention (default 30 days, configurable).

4) Subprocessors: attached is the current registry (redwood_subprocessors_20270603.xlsx). We'll agree to notify ACME 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors and offer an escalation path for objections.

5) E-sign: we can execute via DocuSign or AdobeSign — whichever your legal prefers. I recommend DocuSign for the initial run since it preserves redline history in the envelope.

If you send redlines, I'll do a rapid in-house review and route to our CISO if anything looks like a security exception.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Eli / team —

Thanks for the redline. High-level response to the three asks:

- Subprocessor notice: we can extend notification to 45 days for ACME and agree to provide the reason for any subcontracting along with security attestations.
- Embeddings training: Redwood will not use ACME-specific embeddings to further train models unless ACME provides explicit opt-in. We'll add a carve-out for aggregated, de-identified aggregate metrics that are not reversible.
- Telemetry for product improvement: we will only surface aggregated metrics; any metric that includes identifiers will be pseudonymized before use. Operational access controls and a quarterly transparency report will be added to the DPA as schedule.

Rishi, can you confirm the pseudonymization approach and retention timeline?

Marissa
